title: Derived geometric stalk of a constant local model
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $A$ a commutative ring. Use the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], their constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and let $E^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules; write $\underline{E^\bullet}_U$ for its termwise constant sheaf complex [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Suppose an isomorphism $\alpha:f^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{E^\bullet}_U$ is given, where $f^{-1}$ is the exact constant-coefficient module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For every geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], put $\bar x=f\circ\bar u$. Applying the exact stalk functor termwise to representatives of $\alpha$ gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}E^\bullet$ in $D(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Here $K_{\bar x}$ is the derived object obtained by termwise geometric stalks; its coefficient ring is identified with $A$ by the constant-section stalk map. No boundedness, finiteness, constructibility or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09BI (lemma-connected-ctf-locally-constant), proof: the constant ring complexes on overlapping etale cover members are identified by a geometric stalk. Agent extraction of this derived-stalk comparison, using exact stalks and module-linear inverse-image composition.

proof.text: Put $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and define $T_{\bar u}(G)=\Gamma(P,\bar u^{-1}G)$ on constant-$A$ module sheaves. The geometric-point comparison identifies this functor with the geometric stalk on underlying abelian groups. It is $A$-linear: for each $a\in A$, naturality applied to the abelian-sheaf endomorphism $m_a:G\to G$ identifies its action on both sides, and inverse image takes this action to the module action specified in the exact module inverse-image theorem. The identification of the coefficient-ring stalk with $A$ sends the germ of the constant section $a$ to $a$. The point-site global-sections functor and $\bar u^{-1}$ are exact, so $T_{\bar u}$ is exact. Now the module-linear composition comparison $\bar u^{-1}f^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}(f\circ\bar u)^{-1}G$ induces, on global sections and then via the point comparison, an $A$-linear natural isomorphism $T_{\bar u}(f^{-1}G)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{\bar x}(G)=G_{\bar x}$. Apply it in every degree of a complex: naturality with respect to each differential makes it an isomorphism of complexes.

proof.text: Apply the exact-functor derived-factorization theorem to $f^{-1}$ and to the exact functors $T_{\bar u}$ and $T_{\bar x}$ of Step 1. Their termwise complex functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce functors on the unbounded derived categories. The comparison of Step 1 descends through the localization: its naturality holds for chain maps and therefore also for their inverses when these become invertible. Thus $T_{\bar u,D}(f^{-1}_DK)\cong T_{\bar x,D}(K)=K_{\bar x}$. Apply $T_{\bar u,D}$ to the given derived isomorphism $\alpha$, and compose with the inverse of this comparison to obtain $K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{\bar u,D}(\underline{E^\bullet}_U)$. A functor sends the inverse of $\alpha$ to an inverse, so this remains an isomorphism even when $\alpha$ is represented by localized maps rather than by a chain isomorphism. The cited factorization theorem applies to arbitrary complexes; no boundedness is used.

proof.text: By the termwise-constant-complex definition, degree $n$ of $\underline{E^\bullet}_U$ is the constant sheaf $\underline{E^n}_U$. The constant-stalk theorem gives an additive isomorphism $\gamma_n:E^n\to(\underline{E^n}_U)_{\bar u}$, $e\mapsto\operatorname{germ}(\iota_U(e))$. This is $A$-linear because multiplication by $a\in A$ on the constant sheaf is induced from $e\mapsto ae$ on the constant presheaf, so $a\gamma_n(e)=\gamma_n(ae)$. Likewise the sheaf map $\underline{d^n}$ is induced from $d^n:E^n\to E^{n+1}$, giving $(\underline{d^n})_{\bar u}\gamma_n(e)=\operatorname{germ}(\iota_U(d^ne))=\gamma_{n+1}(d^ne)$. Hence the $\gamma_n$ assemble to an $A$-linear chain isomorphism $E^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}(\underline{E^\bullet}_U)_{\bar u}$. Its inverse, followed by localization, identifies $T_{\bar u,D}(\underline{E^\bullet}_U)$ with $E^\bullet$ in $D(A)$.

source.place: Lemma 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact) (2), Definition 040R (definition-stalk); canonical constant germs applied to the local constant models in Lemma 09BI (lemma-connected-ctf-locally-constant).

proof.text: Compose the isomorphism of Step 2 with the inverse of the constant-germ chain isomorphism of Step 3 in $D(A)$. This gives $K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}E^\bullet$. Every map used is $A$-linear. The representative description is precisely termwise stalk evaluation followed by these canonical comparisons; descent through localization in Step 2 ensures that it is independent of how the given $\alpha$ is represented.
